items.title: George "Kid Sheik" Colar Interview, 1958-07-20
items.q: I got a little more experience from Wooden Joe because I used to go by his house. We'd stay there and I'd have more time with him. Oh, yes. And try and learn how to execute the horn

ctx.x: Was there anybody in particular who taught you to play your instrument, trumpet? Not right off the reel.

I just flew around with the horn and used to put a kuzit, one of the kuzit, and just blowed like I was playing the trumpet. Mark beats the trumpet and every year, the kuzit, the kuzit. And Faisal and I got around Chris and them. He told me to come to his house and taught me how to try to blow it. Didn't have much time to waste with me. Every time I blew that wood we go, I'd start to drink. That was the most of the thing, was drinking. In fact, I got a little more experience from Wooden Joe because I used to go by…
But before we go on, I'm sure if I would ask for Mr. Kuller somewhere among the musicians, nobody would know your name. Your name actually among musicians is Sheik, isn't it?

items.title: George "Kid Sheik" Colar Interview, 1959-01-20
items.q: ...around Wooden Joe. ...and then he'd tell me how to start me and how to fill the horn and blow. And blow and I'd follow him around.

ctx.x: Just a second. Okay, you and your violins, I don't see why you don't. Well, anyway...

Yeah, I had that old beat up cornet it was. I just remember who I got that cornet from. I just remember who I got that cornet from. One old trumpet player, yeah, the cornet. I just remember it in there. It's been a good while. Anyway, I was around about ten or eleven years old then. And I fooled around and I could never blow the thing. I used to put a kazut in it. I used a mouthpiece to put a kazut. The mouthpiece to put a kazut? No, I'd put the kazut in the, you know, where the mouthpiece goes. You see, in the…
They have a lot of guys that just play piano and guitar and all kind of odd instruments serenading like that.
